title: From health scores to decisions
subtitle: Five composite scores built from the per-cluster metrics with weights that live in a database table, feeding the pressure model that decides what the corpus does next

stats.label: raw metrics per cluster, a diagnosis rather than a decision
members, above which the spectral metrics are left null
per composite and metric holds every weight

lede: Thirty-eight metrics per cluster is a diagnosis. The decisions, split this cluster, merge those two, leave that one alone, are made inside the database by a pressure model, and the pressure model reads five composite scores rather than thirty-eight raw values. This is how the composites are built and why their weights are data rather than code. Each composite is a weighted average over a named subset of the metrics, and each subset answers one question about the cluster. A metric can be missing for a cluster: the spectral metrics above 2,000 members, a question-and-answer metric on a cluster with no pairs, a neighbourhood metric on a cluster with no neighbours yet.
quote: A composite that treated a missing value as zero would punish the cluster for the gap.
evidence: Embedding analytics and cluster metrics: 38 raw metrics per cluster folded into five composite health scores that a pressure model reads to split, merge or hold a cluster.
Robust scoring with missing data: skip-null averaging that renormalises over the weights present and stores the metric count beside each composite instead of reading a gap as zero.
Configuration as audited data: composite weights held as one row per composite and metric in PostgreSQL, read by both the CPU reference and the SQL that computes the composites.
Data-driven automation: typed functions inside the database act on split, merge and hold pressures derived from kernel metrics, every step reproducible from the metric definitions.
author: Corey James
